data.name: authority
data.source: searchParams — since `a-lost-authority-is-not-a-refusal`, the sentence a performUndeploy whose account authority is gone redirected back with. Read before anything else and, when present, it replaces the whole page with <AuthorityLost>. It is not a refusal of this removal and does not travel as ?problem=.

components.purpose: Ask one question — stop this agent scanning this market? — with what stops stated before the button, and the coin in the path because the deployment is the thing the page is about.
components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centered column, space-y-4, p-6 — the confirmation-page skeleton. Branch order: not-connected, then authority-lost, then the roster read. h1 'Remove <name> from <coin>?'. refused renders h1 'Cannot undeploy' + the reason (role=alert, untinted text) + an underlined 'Back to the agent' link. Since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` all four describe-reaching branches mount `<CarriedProblem>` unconditionally as the first thing under the h1 — it renders null when there is no carried reason, so every `-with-problem` pairing above is a real rendering rather than a variant somebody has to remember. On refused and roster-unreadable two alerts stack — the carried reason for the click that bounced, then this page's own fresh failure. Destructive on the platform (delete_radar_deployment), reversible in substance — the agent stays configured and can be redeployed, and the consequence says exactly that. NEW since `a-lost-authority-is-not-a-refusal`: `authority-lost` is a fifth top-level branch, taken before the roster is even read, that returns the shared `<AuthorityLost>` and nothing else — no proposal, no form, and deliberately no CarriedProblem even when a ?problem= rode in alongside.
constraints: The page renders whole from one server round trip and holds no client state — the only client code is PerformButton ('use client', useFormStatus), which reports that a submit is in flight and nothing else. A design requiring further client-side interactivity changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.
The removal is performed only after a person confirms against the specific agent and market — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:14-16; the two-request ceremony must survive any relayout.

The consequence and the revision come from a fresh radar read — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:16-17 ('SHALL carry the deployment's current revision from a fresh read'); nothing on this page may render remembered radar state.

Every describe-reaching branch renders the carried reason, not just the ones that can offer a form — `tests/agent/refusals-reach-the-operator.test.ts` asserts one `<CarriedProblem>` per `<main>` in this file. A design that suppresses it on a terminal branch changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.
Where two alerts stack (carried reason above this page's own failure reason), both must stay readable as separate claims.

The authority-lost branch renders no form and no carried problem, on purpose — 'a control that cannot work is not made honest by the sentence above it' (authority-lost.tsx). A design that gives this branch the confirmation back, or dresses it as one more refusal beside the others, changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

components.purpose: Show the refusal that bounced a submitted undeploy back to the person who clicked it — on whichever branch the page then lands.
components.current_implementation: The shared `CarriedProblem` component (src/presentation/components/carried-problem.tsx), extracted by `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` from the ternary that used to be inline on this page. Carries DT-0004's danger treatment unchanged — rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert, opening with a semibold 'Refused: ' prefix so the state is named as well as tinted — and returns null when `problem` is undefined, which is what lets every branch mount it unconditionally.
constraints: role=alert must survive.

The reason shown is the one the platform returned, on the surface acted from — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:32-34. Do not truncate or paraphrase; the string is platform-authored and unbounded, so the block must wrap rather than clip.
A stale removal refused by the revision check must keep reaching the operator rather than looking like success — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:26-29.

Shared by eleven pages now (agent deploy/undeploy/rebind/archive/reactivate, strategy archive/restore/fork, both /pending surfaces, recorder trim) — restyle it in the component, never per page. `tests/agent/refusals-reach-the-operator.test.ts` fails any file that hand-rolls it again.
Rendering nothing when there is no problem is load-bearing — a design must not give it a reserved empty slot or a placeholder.
The 'Refused: ' prefix is part of the treatment — a design may restyle the prefix but must not drop the naming of the state.

components.purpose: Name what stops happening — the agent ceases scanning this market — in the sentence the token was issued against, before the button.
components.current_implementation: rounded-gc-2 border border-consequence-border bg-consequence-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert. DT-0017 has landed: the anonymous border-border-default this was built with is gone and the block now wears the house consequence role, the same one the strategy archive callout and the recorder-trim description already wore.
constraints: The confirmation MUST name what stops: the agent, the market, and that it ceases scanning there — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:15-16 and :23-24. A design must not paraphrase, truncate, or summarize the platform-derived sentence.
The removal is reversible in substance and the consequence says so — it must not be restyled to read as deletion or loss.
Consequence outranks everything on a screen (system.json principle) — this block must not become lighter than the buttons below it.
role=alert must survive.

components.purpose: Carry the undeploy decision: one committing button, one visible way out.

actions.effect: POSTs the server action with agentId, coinId, expectedRevision, confirmationToken; success lands on /agents/[id], refusal redirects back here with ?problem=; a lost account authority redirects back with ?authority= instead, which renders the page as AuthorityLost with no form

components.current_implementation: flex flex-col gap-3 tablet:flex-row tablet:flex-wrap — DT-0017 has landed: the row stacks full-width below the `tablet` breakpoint and only becomes a wrapping row above it, matching the archive page. Four hidden inputs carry the confirmation binding.
constraints: The hidden binding (agentId, coinId, expectedRevision, confirmationToken) is the confirmation ceremony — the form must keep exactly one submit path.
The stacking breakpoint is `tablet`; both controls carry `w-full tablet:w-auto` so the commit and its peer are the same width when stacked. A design must not restore a wrapping row at mobile width.
Cancel must remain a visible peer of the submit, never a text link beneath it (DT-0002 ruling, restated in control.ts).

components.purpose: Commit the removal, named with what stops: 'Stop scanning <coin>'.
components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY constant from control.ts — accent.default bg, min-h-control (44px, DT-0003's token), rounded-gc-2, hover to accent.hover over duration-fast, active holds hover at duration-instant. Since DT-0017 it carries `w-full tablet:w-auto`, so it fills the stacked row on mobile. No pending/loading state between click and redirect. system.json declares this primitive with states [default, hover, active, focused, disabled, loading]; `disabled` and `loading` are declared there as names with no treatment and are implemented by nothing in control.ts, so no form in the product can reach them (#153). The harness half of that is now solved — tests/rendering/support/form-status.ts reaches both states — so what is missing is the look, which is this round's to decide. DT-0022 added the primitive's `disabled` treatment to this constant — bg.sunken ground, text.disabled label, border.subtle edge and cursor not-allowed, stated rather than an opacity. DT-0022 defined the primitive's `disabled` treatment on this constant, but **nothing in the product enters it** — so it is not listed as a state of this surface. system.json declares it and DT-0022 styles it; a surface claiming a state it cannot reach is the same fiction DT-0003 refused for the ghost and danger variants.
constraints: Deliberately NOT danger-styled — DT-0002's ruling, restated in control.ts: the legitimate action is not a hazard; the weight belongs on the consequence block.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_PRIMARY constant in control.ts, shared by every committing submit in the product.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
Focus ring comes from the one global rule in globals.css — do not add a per-element ring.

components.purpose: Keep the deployment and go back to the agent: 'Keep it deployed'.
components.current_implementation: An anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — inline-flex centering, min-h-control, DT-0004's hover (border-strong + bg-sunken over duration-fast; active holds it at duration-instant), plus `w-full tablet:w-auto` since DT-0017. Only the proposal branch wears it; the refused, roster-unreadable and no-such-agent branches still use plain underlined prose links. Where this is an anchor it can never be pending — it submits nothing. Where a surface uses it as a GET submit (the deploy chooser's ask), it can, and system.json's declared `disabled` and `loading` states are unimplemented there too (#153). Recorded on button-primary rather than here, because that is the control a perform runs through.
constraints: Must remain an anchor (pure navigation, no form participation) and a visible peer of the submit.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_SECONDARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).

components.purpose: Tell an operator whose agent did not load whether to wait or to reconnect — and that their agent is not gone.
components.current_implementation: Shared WhyNotLoaded (why-not-loaded.tsx), a plain mt-2 paragraph under the 'Could not load this agent' heading. Two sentences, chosen by cause carried out of the read itself.
constraints: The refused/unreachable distinction must stay two different sentences — a platform that answered and declined is not one that could not be reached.

components.purpose: Say that the account's BattleGrid authority is gone — not that this removal was refused — where the operator was standing when their submit failed.

actions.effect: Anchor to /connect, where a new grant is obtained. Rendered only on remedy-reconnect. It navigates and submits nothing, and it is not the operation that failed — that control stays absent on both branches.

components.current_implementation:
Shared `AuthorityLost` component (src/presentation/components/authority-lost.tsx), also mounted by the agent deploy, undeploy and rebind pages and the strategy rule editor. It replaces the whole page rather than banding the top of one: its own `
`, h1 'Your BattleGrid authority is no longer valid' in text-text-primary, the carried sentence in `rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary` with role=alert — the same treatment CarriedProblem wears — then a text-sm text-text-secondary paragraph: 'Nothing was changed. Until this is fixed, no operation on this account can succeed — including the one you just tried.' **Since `a-remedy-is-a-target-not-a-sentence` (#182) it also takes the deployment's `remedy` and branches on it.** On `reconnect` it appends a `

` holding a BUTTON_SECONDARY anchor to /connect reading 'Connect your BattleGrid account again'. On `repair-the-key` it appends nothing, because replacing an environment variable and restarting a process is not something a link can do. The remedy value is fixed once at src/composition.ts (`config.personal ? 'repair-the-key' : 'reconnect'`) and passed down, so the component never works out which deployment it is on. Nothing has designed any of this; it was built wearing existing tokens, and the anchor reuses the primitive NotConnected already uses for the same purpose rather than introducing a treatment.
constraints: It renders instead of the ceremony, not above it — a design must not turn this into a banner over the proposal. The reason the page has no form is that no call on this account can succeed.

The sentence is passed in and printed verbatim, remedy included — a design must not template it or prefix it. The remedy is **also offered as a target where the deployment has one**: the component links to /connect on `remedy-reconnect` and draws nothing on `remedy-repair-the-key`. A design must not draw that link unconditionally — that is how a personal deployment gets told to press a connect button it does not have — and must not remove it from the reconnect branch, where DT-0006's ruling holds: a remedy is a target, not a sentence.

The two branches are one component and one treatment. The difference between them is whether the anchor renders, not how the page looks. A design that gave the two deployments different layouts would be designing for a distinction the operator can neither see nor change.

It must stay visually distinct from CarriedProblem even though both currently wear danger: one says this attempt was refused and something else may work, the other says nothing will. If a design keeps them identical it should say that is a decision.
role=alert must survive on the reason.
Shared with agent deploy, agent rebind and the strategy rule editor — restyle it in the component, never per page.

components.purpose: Turn away a request without authority, with the one remedy that works: connect.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, and since DT-0006 the connect link is an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — the way in as a target, not a sentence, at the 44px floor with secondary's hover. Used by every authenticated page, so this treatment is inherited everywhere. This is the one branch that does not mount CarriedProblem — it renders before searchParams are read.
constraints: Every no-authority cause renders this same page by design (see design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants.

flows.name: Undeploy an agent from a market
steps: arrive from the agent page with the coin in the path
read what stops, in the platform-derived sentence from a fresh radar read
submit 'Stop scanning <coin>'
land on /agents/[id] with the deployment removed

flows.name: The undeploy is refused after submit
steps: submit
platform refuses (revision moved, not deleted)
redirected back here with ?problem=
the describe re-runs and the problem banner (shared CarriedProblem) states the reason above the fresh proposal

flows.name: The bounce lands on a branch that fails too
steps: submit; the platform refuses and redirects back with ?problem=
the re-describe also refuses, or the roster will not load
the problem banner (shared CarriedProblem) still states why the click was refused, above the fresh reason for this branch — both facts, not one

flows.name: The account's authority is gone
steps: submit 'Stop scanning <coin>'
the platform answers that the connection or credential is no longer valid
performUndeploy's authority-lost arm redirects back to this route with ?authority= — not ?problem=
the page renders <AuthorityLost> alone: the reason, and that nothing was changed and nothing on this account can succeed until it is fixed. No form to retry with.

flows.name: Nothing to remove
steps: the coin carries no deployment, or the radar cannot be read
'Cannot undeploy' states the reason; no token is minted
'Back to the agent' is the way out

flows.name: Walk away
steps: click 'Keep it deployed'
back on /agents/[id], nothing changed

accessibility.notes: The carried problem, consequence, refusal and authority-lost messages all carry role=alert; on a bounced branch two of them are adjacent. The authority-lost branch has an alert and no focusable element at all — it is the one state on this surface with nothing to tab to. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). Every state change is a full navigation; the only client code is PerformButton, which reports that a submit is in flight and nothing else.
